A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the phase behavior of ternary mixtures of γD, βB1, and water is characterized by a significant demix of γD and γB1 and a lowering of the phase-separation temperature upon increasing the βB1 fraction in solution.

we have experimentally and theoretically characterized the phase behavior of the ternary mixture of human lens proteins γD, βB1, and water, and we have determined the magnitude of the interaction energies of γD and γD with βB1, as well as of βB1 with itself.
the phase behavior of the γD/βB1 mixture is determined by the competition between two attractive interactions, γD-γ and γD-β, and one repulsive interaction, β-β.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in order to maintain proteins in the homogeneous state, one should avoid the formation of protein complexes with a high degree of specificity, i.e. with large interaction energies.
the energy of attractive interactions between proteins in the human eye lens is significantly smaller than that of the attractive interactions between water molecules and proteins.
a significant difference in the strength of interprotein attractive interactions is essential for maintaining a homogeneous phase of lens proteins.
